newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares close lower amid corporate moves.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares close lower amid corporate moves.

text.p: Stockholm's bourse closed lower on Monday after opening lower in line with a weaker perfomance on Wall Street and amid a major shakeup in Sweden's corporate sector. It slipped further when New York opened.
The Stockholm general index closed 0.47 percent lower at 2,500.73 after shares worth 3.60 billion crowns changed hands.
Brokers said the key focus was changes at the top of three companies, vehicle maker Volvo, appliance manufacturer Electrolux and industrial engineer Atlas Copco.
"So many leadership changes are always a surprise," said one broker.

Volvo announced chief executive Soren Gyll was to quit at the end of April but stay on the company's board. Volvo share dipped initially but by the close of trade were three crowns higher at 180 crowns.
Gyll will be replaced by head of Electrolux, 45-year-old Leif Johansson.
Electrolux shares benefitted from the news that Michael Treschow, head of Atlas Copco, was to take to the helm. Shares rose as much as 19 crowns but closed 12 up at 438.
Atlas Copco is to be headed by senior executive Giulio Mazzalupi. It shares slipped 0.5 to 169.5 crowns.
Banks S-E-Banken and Nordbanken were actively traded on continuing merger rumours. S-E-Banken closed unchanged at 72.50 crowns while Nordbanken slipped 1.5 to 232 crowns.
Drugs major Astra ended 1.5 crowns higher at 338 crowns, after slipping off a high of 340.5 crowns. Brokers attributed the slip to jitters over U.S. data later in the week.
